title: Jellyfish
subject: A single jellyfish in side view: domed bell with radiating lines, frilled oral arms and long trailing tentacles
style: Natural history plate, engraving-style line work with a screened bell
description: A jellyfish hangs in open water, its domed bell trailing frilled arms and a curtain of beaded tentacles. It has managed for five hundred million years without a brain, which is more than can be said for most of us.

title: Sea Turtle
subject: A sea turtle swimming, seen from above at a slight angle: head, plated shell and two front flippers
style: Natural history plate, engraving-style line work with scale patterns and stipple
description: A sea turtle glides past with its front flippers spread, every scale and shell plate drawn in fine engraved line. It has been doing this for a hundred million years and sees no reason to hurry now.

title: Barn Owl
subject: A barn owl perched on a bare branch, facing the viewer
style: Natural history portrait, fine stipple and screened tone
description: A barn owl sits upright on a dead branch, its pale facial disc turned straight towards you. It has clearly already decided whether you are worth eating.

title: Patagonia
subject: Mountains
style: Halftone engraving
description: Three granite towers rise above a scree valley and a glacial lake, after the Torres del Paine in Chilean Patagonia. They have stood there for some twelve million years and are in no hurry to be anywhere else.

title: Pine on the Cliff
subject: Tree
style: Halftone engraving
description: An old wind-bent pine grows alone from a rocky ledge above a calm bay, with headlands on either side. It has chosen the view over the soil, and seems content with the bargain.

title: Lighthouse
subject: A tall round stone lighthouse with its keeper's cottage on a rocky headland, Atlantic waves breaking below
style: Engraving-style landscape, clustered-dot tone, the ground cut straight with a thin rule under it
description: A slender stone lighthouse and its keeper's cottage stand on a rocky headland while the swell breaks white on the rocks below. It has been keeping the lights on for longer than most utilities.

title: Spiral Shell
subject: A single coiled sea shell seen side on, its ribbed whorls winding in to a fine centre
style: Natural history plate, engraving-style pen lines
description: A coiled shell winds in on itself in ribbed whorls, each turn a little smaller than the last. Its owner built it one chamber at a time and never once needed planning permission.

title: Pufferfish
subject: A spotted pufferfish seen head on, fully inflated, a round ball of spines with two big eyes and a pouting mouth
style: Natural history plate, bold pen line work and spotted pattern
description: A pufferfish faces the viewer fully inflated, its spotted body a ball of spines round two wide eyes and a pout. It swallows water to treble its size, which settles most arguments before they start.

title: Snowy Owl
subject: A snowy owl perched on a bare branch, facing the viewer
style: Natural history portrait in fine ink line, spotted plumage and light screened shading
description: A snowy owl sits square on a bare branch, both yellow eyes fixed on you and both feet locked round the wood. It has the calm of a bird that has never once been cold.

title: Golden Eagle
subject: A golden eagle facing the viewer with both wings raised and spread wide
style: Heraldic natural history study in fine ink line, feather by feather
description: A golden eagle faces straight out with both wings thrown open, every flight feather drawn in its place. It is the posture of a bird that has seen the coat of arms and intends to keep it.

title: Kingfisher
subject: A kingfisher in side portrait, crest raised, long dagger beak pointing right
style: Natural history portrait in ink line and screened shading
description: A kingfisher sits half turned with its crest up and its long straight beak aimed at something only it can see. Somewhere a small fish has just had a very bad idea.

title: Bird's Nest
subject: A round woven bird's nest with five eggs, seen from directly above
style: Natural history study in ink line and screened tone, top-down
description: A round nest of woven grass and twigs holds five pale eggs, seen from straight above. Someone has clearly been very busy, and is not going to say who.

title: Swallowtail Butterfly
subject: A swallowtail butterfly with its wings open, seen from directly above
style: Natural history plate, fine pen line and hatched wing borders
description: A swallowtail butterfly laid flat with its four wings open and its two long tails trailing below. It has spent its whole life looking this symmetrical and would like some credit for it.

title: Moth
subject: A moth with its four wings open, seen from directly above
style: Natural history plate, fine pen line with banded wings
description: A moth laid flat with its wings open, a furry thorax, a striped abdomen and long trailing hind wings. It came all this way for a light bulb and settled for a shirt.

title: Dragonfly
subject: A dragonfly with its four wings spread flat, seen from directly above
style: Natural history plate, fine pen line with lace wing veins
description: A dragonfly laid out flat, four wings of fine lace veins on either side of a long segmented body. It has been flying in much this way for three hundred million years and sees no reason to change now.

title: Bat
subject: A bat seen from the front with both wings spread wide
style: Natural history plate, fine pen line and hatched wing membranes
description: A bat facing you with its wings stretched to their full span, the membrane pulled taut between long finger bones. It would prefer you saw it at dusk, from a distance.

title: Wolf
subject: A grey wolf head and ruff, front view, looking straight out
style: Engraving-style line portrait, fine fur strokes and screened mid-tones
description: A grey wolf looks straight out, ears up and ruff full, drawn in fine fur strokes. It has clearly heard about the sheep.

title: Lion
subject: A male lion head with full mane, front view, looking straight out
style: Engraving-style line portrait, flowing mane strokes
description: A male lion looks straight out from a full, flowing mane, drawn in fine ink strokes. The hair took longer than the hunting.

title: Red Deer Stag
subject: A red deer stag head and neck with two branching antlers, front view
style: Engraving-style pen portrait, fur and antlers in fine strokes
description: A red deer stag faces out under a full set of branching antlers, drawn in fine pen strokes. He grows them fresh every year and still looks smug about it.

title: Brown Bear
subject: A brown bear head and shoulders, front view, looking straight out
style: Engraving-style line portrait, fur strokes and screened mid-tones
description: A brown bear looks straight out with round ears and a broad muzzle, drawn in fine fur strokes. It has the calm of something that sleeps through winter on purpose.

title: Highland Bull
subject: A Highland bull head with two long curved horns and a shaggy coat, front view
style: Engraving-style pen portrait, long hair in flowing strokes
description: A Highland bull stares out from under a shaggy fringe between two wide curved horns, drawn in long pen strokes. The hairstyle is entirely deliberate and not up for discussion.

title: Maple Leaf
subject: A single five-lobed maple leaf, flat in front view, its veins fanning out from the base of a long straight stalk
style: Natural history plate, engraving-style line work
description: One maple leaf lies flat, five toothed lobes spreading from a single point on its long stalk. Each one is drawn as if it might be needed for a flag.

title: Fern Frond
subject: A single upright fern frond in front view: one straight stem with paired, finely toothed leaflets tapering to the tip
style: Natural history plate, engraving-style line work
description: One fern frond stands straight up its stem, its paired leaflets narrowing evenly to a point. Ferns were here long before flowers and have never seen the need to catch up.

title: Pine Cone
subject: A single closed pine cone standing upright in front view, its woody scales overlapping in neat rows to a pointed tip
style: Natural history plate, engraving-style line work
description: A closed pine cone stands on end, row upon row of woody scales stacked to its tip. It will open them only when the weather is dry enough, which shows more sense than most of us manage.

title: Artichoke
subject: A single globe artichoke in front view on a short cut stem, its pointed bracts overlapping in rows, a ruff of leaves at the base
style: Natural history plate, engraving-style line work
description: One globe artichoke stands on its cut stem, the pointed bracts closing in over the heart. It is, strictly speaking, a thistle that never got round to flowering.

title: Sunflower Head
subject: A single sunflower head seen face on: a round disc of seeds in crossing spirals, ringed by two rows of pointed petals
style: Natural history plate, engraving-style line work
description: A sunflower seen head on, its seeds packed in crossing spirals inside a double ring of petals. The spirals follow the Fibonacci numbers, though the sunflower has never been asked to show its working.

title: Pomegranate
subject: A pomegranate cut in half, the open face with its chambers of red flesh and the crown at the top
style: Engraving-style line drawing, fine hatching on the rind
description: A pomegranate sliced clean through the middle, its crown standing up like a small, slightly surprised hat. Considerably tidier than eating one.

title: Fly Agaric
subject: Three fly agaric mushrooms, two tall and one small, with spotted caps and gills, growing in a tuft of grass
style: Engraving-style line drawing with fine hatching on the gills
description: Three fly agarics stand in the grass, caps spotted, gills finely ruled. Lovely to look at and best left exactly there.

title: Lotus Flower
subject: A lotus in full bloom seen from the front, layered pointed petals on a single stem
style: Pen-and-ink line drawing, petals ruled with fine parallel lines
description: A lotus opens in tiers of pointed petals, each ruled from tip to base. It rises out of the mud and still manages to look like this.

title: Rose
subject: A single rose bloom seen head on, petals spiralling into a tight centre
style: Engraving-style line drawing with a fine screen in the shaded folds
description: One rose seen straight on, petals turning inward to a tight spiral at its heart. No thorns were included, which is more than most roses can say.

title: Lemon Branch
subject: A lemon branch with two ripe lemons hanging among glossy leaves
style: Engraving-style botanical plate in clustered-dot tone
description: Two lemons hang from a single leafy branch, drawn in the manner of an old botanical plate. Life handed it lemons and it made a print.

title: Alpine Peak
subject: Mountains
style: Halftone engraving
description: A lone pyramid of rock and snow rises above the lower ridges, one face lit and one in shadow, fading into the paper at its feet. It has been standing perfectly still for a few million years and shows no sign of getting bored.

title: Alpine Lake
subject: Mountains
style: Halftone engraving
description: A still mountain lake holds the reflection of the snowy peaks behind it, framed by dark pines on both shores. The water is perfectly calm, which is more than can be said for anyone who has tried swimming in it.

title: Desert Cliffs
subject: Landscapes
style: Halftone engraving
description: A long wall of flat-topped sandstone cliffs runs into a dry valley dotted with desert scrub. The rock was laid down one thin layer at a time, which is one way to avoid being rushed.

title: Waterfall
subject: Landscapes
style: Halftone engraving
description: A single tall fall drops between walls of dense fern and rock into a misty pool. The water has been taking the same route down for a very long time and sees no reason to change.

title: Pine Forest in Mist
subject: Trees
style: Halftone engraving
description: Tall straight pines stand in rows, the near trunks dark and sharp, the far ones lost in morning fog. Visibility is poor, but the trees have never needed to go anywhere.

title: Sea Stacks
subject: Three tall rock sea stacks rising from the sea off a rocky shore, surf around boulders in the foreground
style: Engraving-style landscape vignette, clustered-dot tone fading to nothing at the edges
description: Three weathered sea stacks stand off a rocky shore with the surf working at their feet. The sea has been carving them for millennia and shows no sign of finishing.

title: Breaking Wave
subject: One tall curling ocean wave breaking, its hollow barrel and curled foam crest over a rolling sea
style: Woodblock-style wave in flowing lines, clustered-dot tone fading to nothing at the edges
description: A single tall wave curls over into a hollow barrel, its crest breaking into fingers of foam above a rolling sea. Surfers call this ideal, sailors rather less so.

title: Rocky Islet
subject: A small islet of rounded boulders in a calm sea, one tall windswept pine on top and a smaller one behind, reflected in the still water
style: Engraving-style landscape vignette, clustered-dot tone fading to nothing at the edges
description: A windswept pine grows from a heap of rounded boulders in a flat calm sea, with a younger one keeping it company behind. Room for two, no ferry.

title: Chalk Cliffs
subject: Pale sheer sea cliffs in stepped layers running down to a calm sea, a scatter of rocks in the shallows
style: Engraving-style landscape vignette, clustered-dot tone fading to nothing at the edges
description: Pale cliffs fall in sheer stepped walls to a flat sea, with a few dark rocks scattered in the shallows. The coastline retreats a little every winter and never asks permission.

title: Fishing Hut on Stilts
subject: A gabled wooden hut with a balcony standing on tall stilts over still water, a jetty beside it and its reflection below
style: Engraving-style vignette, clustered-dot tone fading to nothing at the edges
description: A plank hut with a balcony stands on tall stilts above flat water, a jetty at its side and its reflection beneath. Commute: one ladder.

title: Full Moon
subject: The full moon, one disc, front view: the near side with its dark maria, bright highlands and scattered craters
style: Tonal engraving-style plate in a clustered-dot screen
description: The near side of the full moon, its dark seas and pale highlands drawn as a single disc in a fine dot screen. It has shown us exactly this face for four billion years, which is commitment of a kind.

title: Jupiter
subject: The planet Jupiter, one sphere, front view: horizontal cloud belts with swirls and small oval storms, lit from the left
style: Tonal engraving-style plate in a clustered-dot screen
description: Jupiter in banded cloud, lit from one side with its night side falling away into shadow. Eleven times the width of Earth and still mostly weather.

title: Iceberg
subject: One tall jagged iceberg in calm sea, front view, its reflection running down into still water
style: Tonal engraving-style plate in a clustered-dot screen, faded to the edges
description: A single iceberg stands in flat calm, one face lit and one in shadow, doubled in the water below. Most of it is underwater, as with most things worth knowing about.

title: Quartz Crystal Cluster
subject: A cluster of quartz crystals growing from a rough rock base: one tall six-sided point in the middle, smaller points around it
style: Mineral plate in one ink, screened line work
description: A cluster of quartz points rising from its matrix, the tallest a clean six-sided prism. Silicon dioxide, arranged with more patience than anyone has ever had.

title: Glacier
subject: A mountain glacier seen from its foot, a river of ice running up a steep valley between rock ridges towards distant peaks
style: Tonal landscape in a clustered-dot screen, faded to the edges
description: A glacier fills its valley in long folded bands of ice, cut by crevasses and walled in by rock. It is moving the whole time, just not in any hurry you would notice.

title: Anchor
subject: An old iron ship's anchor standing upright, with two curved arms at the crown, a double stock near the top and a ring on its shank
style: Engraving-style line work, cross-hatching on the iron, white lines on the tee
description: An iron anchor stands upright, its two arms curving out from the crown below a long shank and a pair of stocks. It has never once been the life of the party, which is rather the point.

title: Oil Lantern
subject: An old metal oil lantern with a domed cap and finial, a glass chimney behind turned guard bars, an oil font inside and a broad turned base
style: Engraving-style line work with screened shading on the metal, white lines on the tee
description: An old metal lantern stands on its turned base, the glass held behind slim guard bars beneath a domed cap. It is waiting, with some patience, for somebody to bring a match.

title: Hourglass
subject: A tall glass hourglass between a turned wooden cap and base, sand heaped in both bulbs and a thin stream at the waist
style: Engraving-style line work, hatching on the wood and stipple in the sand, white lines on the tee
description: A tall hourglass stands between a turned cap and base, its sand piled in both bulbs and a thin stream running at the waist. It is the only clock that never needs its batteries changed, only turning over.

title: Coiled Fossil
subject: A single coiled fossil shell seen side on, thick ribs radiating across its whorls to a small tight centre
style: Natural history plate, engraving-style pen lines
description: A fossil shell coils in on itself, its ribs fanning out across each whorl to a thick rounded rim. It has kept its shape for rather longer than most of us keep a New Year's resolution.

title: Sea Snail Shell
subject: A single round sea snail shell seen from above, its body whorl curling in to a small spire, the surface lined with fine growth marks
style: Natural history plate, engraving-style pen lines
description: A round sea snail shell curls in on itself, fine growth lines running out from the spire to the rim. It is the kind of house that moves with its owner and never needs a removal van.

title: Sea Urchin
subject: A single sea urchin seen from above, a knobbed centre ringed by hundreds of long radiating spines
style: Natural history plate, engraving-style pen lines
description: A sea urchin seen from above, its knobbed centre ringed by long spines radiating out in every direction. It has no brain to speak of and still manages never to be stepped on twice.

title: Chambered Shell
subject: A single coiled sea shell seen side on, its whorls divided into rows of curved chambers winding in to a small centre
style: Natural history plate, engraving-style pen lines
description: A coiled shell winds in to a tight centre, every whorl divided into a row of curved chambers. Its builder added a new room each time it grew and moved into the latest one, leaving the rest empty.

title: Wood Owl
subject: A round-faced wood owl perched on a bare branch, facing the viewer
style: Natural history portrait in fine screened tone, streaked plumage and soft shading
description: A round-faced owl sits square on a bare branch, both dark eyes fixed on you and both feet locked round the wood. It looks like it has already decided what you are and is merely waiting to be proved right.

title: Falcon
subject: The head and shoulders of a pale, heavily spotted falcon in profile, looking left
style: Natural history portrait in fine screened tone, spotted plumage and a hooked beak
description: A pale falcon in profile, its breast scattered with dark spots and its hooked beak turned to the left. It wears the expression of a bird that has already timed your descent.

title: Toucan
subject: A toucan perched on a broken stump, seen from the side with its great curved beak raised
style: Natural history plate in fine screened tone, glossy dark body and pale throat
description: A toucan sits on a broken stump, its huge curved beak tipped up over a pale throat and a dark, glossy body. The beak is mostly air, which is more than can be said for most statements.

title: Banded Moth
subject: A moth with its four wings open, seen from directly above
style: Natural history plate, fine line with banded, scalloped wings
description: A moth laid flat with its wings open, dark bands across every wing, scalloped hind edges and a furry striped body. It keeps night hours and will be wearing yours.

title: Lace Wings
subject: A winged insect with four clear lace-veined wings open, seen from directly above
style: Fine pen line, a dense net of veins in clear wings
description: A slender winged insect seen from above, four broad clear wings ruled into a fine lace of veins around a long segmented body. All that net and still nothing to catch.

title: Butterfly
subject: A butterfly with its four wings open, seen from directly above
style: Natural history plate, clean line with fine veins and a scalloped border
description: A butterfly pinned open, broad veined wings with a dark scalloped border and a row of pale spots. It has been seen from above all its life and has made its peace with that.

title: Spotted Beetle
subject: A round spotted beetle seen from directly above, shell closed
style: Natural history plate, bold line with a polka-dot domed shell
description: A round beetle seen from above, its domed shell split down the middle and covered in dots of every size. It did not count its spots and would rather you did not either.

title: Spider Web
subject: An orb spider web, front view, hanging on one thread, no spider
style: Fine pen line, radiating spokes and a ladder of spiral threads
description: An orb web hung on a single thread, sixteen-odd spokes and a spiral laid rung by rung. The spider has stepped out and left the place tidy.

title: Elephant
subject: An African elephant head, front view, ears spread, tusks and trunk hanging straight
style: Engraving-style line portrait, fine wrinkle lines and screened mid-tones
description: An African elephant faces straight out with its ears fanned wide and its trunk hanging plumb. It is listening, and it will remember.

title: Horse
subject: A pale horse head and neck, front view, ears pricked, forelock and loose mane
style: Pen portrait, flowing hair strokes for the mane and screened mid-tones
description: A pale horse faces straight out, ears up, its mane loose at both sides of the neck. It has been told there are no apples and does not believe it.

title: Snow Leopard
subject: A snow leopard head and ruff, front view, pale eyes, spotted fur and whiskers
style: Pen portrait, fine fur strokes, clear rosette spots and screened mid-tones
description: A snow leopard looks straight out with pale eyes, its spotted ruff full and its whiskers spread. It has been sitting on that ridge for some hours and sees no reason to move.

title: Bison
subject: A bison head, front view, two short curved horns, thick shaggy woolly hair
style: Pen portrait, flowing hair strokes over the whole head and screened mid-tones
description: A bison faces straight out under a great cap of shaggy wool, its two short horns curving up. It does not charge often, but it would like you to keep that in mind.

title: Gorilla
subject: A gorilla head, front view, crested brow, deep-set eyes, broad nose and closed mouth
style: Pen portrait, fine hair strokes over the head and cheeks, wrinkle lines on the face
description: A gorilla looks straight out from under a heavy brow, the hair swept back over its crown. It has listened to the whole proposal and remains unconvinced.

title: Baobab
subject: A single old baobab tree drawn whole, a tall thick trunk with knotholes and furrowed bark, short crooked branches with tufted foliage, standing on a small patch of ground
style: Natural history plate, engraving-style pen work
description: One baobab stands on its own scrap of ground, its great knotted trunk carrying a crown of short crooked branches. It has been there long enough to have seen most things twice.

title: Gnarled Tree
subject: A single old gnarled tree drawn whole, a twisted knotted trunk with hollows and furrowed bark, crooked branches carrying tufted foliage, roots spread on a small patch of ground
style: Natural history plate, engraving-style pen work
description: One old tree twists up from a scrap of ground, its trunk knotted and hollowed by long years of weather. It has clearly given up on growing straight and is doing very well without it.

title: Weeping Willow
subject: A single weeping willow drawn whole, a straight ridged trunk, long hanging strands of thin leaves falling in two curtains, roots spread over a small patch of grass
style: Natural history plate, engraving-style pen work
description: One weeping willow lets its long strands fall in two curtains either side of a straight trunk. It looks sad only to those who have never sat under one in July.

title: Bonsai Pine
subject: A single pine grown in bonsai style, drawn whole, a twisting trunk of furrowed bark, flat layered pads of needles on crooked branches, roots gripping a rock
style: Natural history plate, engraving-style pen work
description: One pine in the bonsai manner winds up from a rock, its needles held in flat, layered pads. Centuries of patience have gone into a tree that fits on a table.

title: Palm Tree
subject: A single tall palm tree drawn whole, a slender straight trunk with fine ring lines, a full crown of long arching feathered fronds, standing on a small patch of sand
style: Natural history plate, engraving-style line work
description: One palm stands tall on a scrap of sand, its long feathered fronds falling from a single crown. It has the composure of something that has never once had to rake leaves.

title: King Protea
subject: A king protea flower head seen from the front, a cup of pointed bracts round a domed centre, on a short stem with leathery leaves
style: Pen-and-ink line drawing, bracts outlined and ruled with fine lines
description: A king protea opens its crown of pointed bracts around a dense, silky centre. It grows back after bush fires, which is more than most of us manage after a bad week.

title: Flowering Stem
subject: Three open five-petalled flowers on a slender branching stem, petals ruled with fine veins
style: Pen-and-ink line drawing, every petal ruled from tip to centre with fine parallel lines
description: Three open blooms on one slender stem, each petal ruled vein by vein from the tip to the heart. They seem perfectly happy without a name.

title: Grass Plume
subject: A feathery plume of grass on three bare stalks, long fine blades fanning out at the top
style: Line drawing in one ink, every blade a fine line
description: A plume of grass on three bare stalks, its long blades fanning upwards like a quill. It has never been asked to make bread and would like to keep it that way.

title: Cherry Branch
subject: A leafy branch with three dark cherries hanging on long stalks among serrated, veined leaves
style: Screened tonal drawing in one ink, like a hand-coloured plate printed in black
description: Three ripe cherries hang on long stalks from a branch of serrated, veined leaves. The birds have not found them yet, which is the only reason this drawing exists.

title: Lavender
subject: A bunch of lavender, eight flower spikes on slender stems with a few narrow leaves, the stems gathered at the bottom
style: Line drawing in one ink, the spikes screened and the stems drawn as fine lines
description: A bunch of lavender, each spike a column of tiny flowers on a slender stem. It smells of summer and drawers full of linen, though the shirt itself will not.

title: Volcano
subject: Volcano
style: Halftone engraving
description: A steep volcanic cone sends a single column of cloud straight up over a stony plain, lit from the left and dark on its right flank. It is letting off steam, which is more than most of us manage so calmly.

title: Terraced Valley
subject: Terraced fields
style: Halftone engraving
description: A long valley of stepped, contoured fields runs back to a small village and a line of bare mountains, with tall grass in the foreground. Someone has gone to a great deal of trouble to make a hillside flat in instalments.

title: Savanna
subject: Savanna with an acacia tree
style: Halftone engraving
description: A flat-topped umbrella acacia stands over a wide grass plain, three smaller acacias and a line of low hills behind it. It has the only shade for miles and appears to know it.

title: Rock Pinnacles
subject: Rock pinnacles over a river
style: Halftone engraving
description: Tall pointed rock spires rise from wooded banks on either side of a still river, with one small rowing boat on the water and paler peaks behind. The boat seems in no hurry, which is wise given how long the rocks have been waiting.

title: Aurora Over Mountains
subject: Aurora over snowy mountains
style: Halftone engraving
description: A broad band of northern lights arcs across a starry sky above a range of snowy peaks and a dark lake edged with pines. It is the most dependable light show in the north, apart from all the nights it does not turn up.

title: Windmill
subject: An old stone tower windmill with three long wooden sails and a cottage beside it, a cobbled path through long grass in front
style: Engraving-style landscape, clustered-dot tone, the ground ending in a straight line under an open sky
description: A tapering stone windmill stands over long grass, a low cottage and trees at its side and a worn path to the door. It has lost a sail somewhere along the way and carries on regardless.

title: Hilltop Monastery
subject: A small stone monastery with a bell tower and a rounded apse on top of a boulder-strewn crag, a stone stair climbing to it past a gatehouse, tall pines either side, mountains far behind
style: Engraving-style landscape, clustered-dot tone, under a round-topped window with a fine keyline
description: A stone monastery with a bell tower sits on top of a rocky crag, reached by one long stair from a gatehouse below. Visitors are welcome, provided they have the knees for it.

title: Stone Cottage
subject: An old two-storey cottage of rough fieldstone with a tiled roof and two tall stone chimneys, a cobbled path through long grass to the door, bare trees behind
style: Engraving-style landscape, clustered-dot tone, the ground ending in a straight line under an open sky
description: A fieldstone cottage with two chimneys and a crooked roof stands at the end of a cobbled path through long grass. Built to last several centuries, and so far managing it.

title: Old Castle
subject: An old castle gatehouse between two crenellated towers, a pointed arch over the gate, a field of tumbled stone blocks in front and low hills behind
style: Engraving-style landscape, clustered-dot tone, the ground ending in a straight line under an open sky
description: An old castle gatehouse stands between two square towers, its pointed arch open over a field of fallen blocks. The gate has not been locked for some time, and nobody seems to mind.

title: Mountain Hut
subject: A small weathered plank hut with a steep gabled roof among tall pines, a field of boulders in front and jagged mountain peaks behind
style: Engraving-style landscape, clustered-dot tone, a complete rectangular scene in a fine keyline
description: A plank hut with a steep roof sits among pines below a ridge of jagged peaks, a field of boulders at its door. The view is excellent, and the path is entirely rocks.

title: Total Solar Eclipse
subject: A total solar eclipse: the moon's black disc with the sun's corona streaming out round it in fine rays
style: Tonal engraving-style plate in a clustered-dot screen
description: The moon covering the sun exactly, with the corona fanning out in fine rays round the black disc. A coincidence of size and distance that only works for now, so best enjoyed while it lasts.

title: Meteor Shower
subject: A meteor shower over rolling hills: many shooting stars streaking across the night sky above a valley and dark fir trees
style: Tonal engraving-style plate in a clustered-dot screen
description: Shooting stars streak across the night sky above rolling hills and a few dark firs. Mostly grains of dust burning up, which is more of an entrance than most of us manage.

title: Lightning Storm
subject: A thunderstorm over a flat grassy plain: a forked lightning bolt under heavy cloud, a track running to the horizon
style: Tonal engraving-style plate in a clustered-dot screen
description: A forked bolt drops out of a heavy storm cloud onto open grassland, with a track running off to the horizon. The road ahead is clear, which is more than can be said for the forecast.

title: Rocky Planet
subject: One rocky planet, a single globe lit from the upper left, with craters and long rifts across its surface
style: Tonal engraving-style plate in a clustered-dot screen
description: A rocky world lit from one side, its craters and long rifts catching the light before the globe turns into shadow. No atmosphere to speak of, and nobody to complain about it.

title: Vintage Camera
subject: An old box camera seen from the front, with a ringed lens in the middle, a viewfinder hood on top and two winding knobs at its shoulders
style: Line work with fine screened texture on the body and rings round the lens, white lines on the tee
description: A boxy old camera looks straight back at you over its one large lens. It has seen everything and kept all of it to itself.

title: Coffee Pot
subject: A round-bellied metal coffee pot in side view, a long swan-neck spout on the left, one looped handle on the right, a stepped lid with a small knob, on a flared foot
style: Line work with screened shading on the polished metal, white lines on the tee
description: A plump metal coffee pot with a swan-neck spout and a lid like a little hat. It has poured a great many second cups and kept count of none of them.

title: Aviator Goggles
subject: A pair of old flying goggles seen from the front, two round rimmed lenses in a padded mask with a stud at the bridge, the strap looping round above and below
style: Line work with screened shading on the mask and lenses, white lines on the tee
description: A pair of round flying goggles faces the front, strap looped about them as if just taken off. From some angles they look faintly amused, which is fair enough.

title: Rope Knot
subject: A round ball of laid rope wound tight on itself, an eye spliced at the top and the tail of the rope hanging below
style: Engraving-style line work, every strand drawn along its twist, white lines on the tee
description: A ball of three-strand rope worked tight on itself, hung from a small eye with its tail let go below. Somebody on watch had a great deal of time and rather a lot of rope.

title: Seahorse Study
subject: One large seahorse in side view, spiny crest, ridged body rings, long snout and curled tail, with a small outline sketch of a seahorse and a sketch of a fan-shaped fin beside it
style: Natural history study sheet, fine pen hatching
description: A seahorse curls its tail beneath a ridged, spiny body while two smaller sketches sit at its side like notes in a margin. It holds its pose better than most sitters, being largely made of armour.

title: Steam Locomotive
subject: An early steam locomotive in side elevation: a long round boiler, tall chimney and two domes on top, three spoked wheels joined by a rod, buffers at both ends, standing on a thin ground line
style: Technical side elevation, engraved line with a fine screen
description: An early steam engine stands side on, its tall chimney at the front and three spoked wheels linked by a single rod. It looks ready to leave on time, which is more than can be said for most of its descendants.

title: Cliff Village
subject: A dense village of old stone houses stacked up a steep sea cliff, arched windows, a balcony, long stone stairs climbing through the houses, rocks and shrubs below and the sea at the left
style: Pen and ink town view, fine hatching, the ground ending in a straight line
description: Old houses climb a sea cliff one on top of another, joined by a long flight of stone steps. Getting the shopping home is, one assumes, its own form of exercise.

title: Acoustic Guitar Study
subject: One acoustic guitar with a cutaway body, round sound hole, pickguard, bridge, fretted neck and headstock with tuning pegs, standing upright between round and boxed detail drawings of its parts
style: Patent study sheet, white line on black
description: An acoustic guitar stands upright in white line, flanked by round and square close-ups of its workings. Nobody has yet asked it to play Wonderwall, and it would like to keep it that way.

title: Lobster Study
subject: A single lobster seen from directly above, both great claws open, walking legs spread, antennae swept back and the tail fan closed
style: Natural history plate, engraving-style stipple and line
description: A lobster laid out from above, claws open and every shell plate stippled in fine dots. It looks ready to argue with the plate it was drawn on.

title: Airship
subject: A fanciful airship in side view: a great ribbed gas envelope with pointed ends, a web of rigging lines and a multi-deck ship's hull hanging beneath it
style: Victorian technical engraving, fine pen lines
description: A gridded balloon lifts an entire steamship by a curtain of ropes. Somebody decided the sea was the slow way round.

title: Domes and Minarets
subject: A great domed mosque with four slender pencil minarets, seen from above over a crowded old town of tiled roofs and a paved square, the city running back to low hills
style: Pen-and-ink townscape, fine line with shadowed hatching
description: Domes stack on domes and four minarets rise over a jumble of old rooftops. Three small figures cross the square, unbothered by the view.

title: Gramophone
subject: An antique wind-up gramophone in three-quarter view: a stepped wooden cabinet on four feet, the turntable and sound box on top, and a great fluted horn flaring up and out
style: Engraving-style line drawing, printed as white line on black
description: A gramophone raises its fluted horn over a stepped wooden cabinet. It plays one record at a time and has never once asked to be updated.

title: Crab Study
subject: A spiny crab seen from above with its claws raised, its shell drawn in outline above and two detail sketches below
style: Natural history study sheet, fine engraved line and stipple
description: A bristling crab from above, two great claws raised over its back and eight jointed walking legs, with an outline of its shell and two detail sketches. It is holding both claws up, which is either a greeting or a warning.

title: Vintage Car
subject: A 1920s touring car with its hood up, in plain side elevation on a thin ground line
style: Technical side elevation, fine black line with light hatching
description: A four-door touring car of the twenties in exact side view, spoked wheels, folding hood, long bonnet and running board. It has not needed a service since about 1931.

title: Mansard Rooftops
subject: A crowd of old town houses with mansard roofs, dormers and chimney pots under one spire, seen from a high window
style: Dense pen and ink town view, fine line and hatching, the ground cut on a straight line
description: Steep slate mansards, dormer windows, iron balconies and forests of chimney pots climbing towards a single spire. Everyone up there has a view and nobody has a lift.

title: Microscope Study
subject: An antique compound microscope large in the centre, with its eyepieces, objectives and fittings drawn small around it
style: Patent study sheet, white chalk-like line and hatching on black
description: A brass compound microscope with its coarse and fine focus, two stages and a heavy foot, ringed by sketches of its eyepieces and fittings. Wear it to look closely at things.

title: Fish Study
subject: A single ocean fish swimming at a slant, with a tall ribbed sail of a dorsal fin, a deep forked tail and fine net-like scales
style: Natural history plate, engraving-style pen lines
description: A long ocean fish cuts down through the water with its sail of a fin raised and every scale drawn in. It looks entirely certain of where it is going, which puts it ahead of most of us.

title: Steel Sphere
subject: A riveted steel sphere in elevation, banded round its middle, with a round porthole, a ladder up its side and fittings on top and below
style: Technical elevation, engraving-style pen lines
description: A banded steel sphere hangs in elevation, its one round porthole set in the middle band and a ladder climbing its curve. Whoever drew it left out what it is for, which is either modesty or a secret.

title: Brownstone Street
subject: A row of old brownstone town houses seen at an angle, with stone stoops, iron railings, balconies, carved window heads and a street tree
style: Pen and ink street drawing, fine line and hatching, the ground ending in a straight line
description: A terrace of brownstones climbs five storeys above a run of stone stoops, every window capped with its own carved hood. Each stoop seats two neighbours comfortably and an opinion about parking indefinitely.

title: Spiral Shell
subject: One large thin-walled spiral seashell seen from the side, a tight coil at its centre opening into a wide flaring whorl, fine radiating ribs and a row of small knobs along the keel
style: Natural history plate, engraving-style line work
description: A single spiral shell unrolls from a tight coil into a broad ribbed sweep, its keel picked out in small knobs. Whoever lived in it has moved somewhere with more cupboard space.

title: Antique Telescope
subject: One antique refracting telescope with a finder scope, eyepiece and dew cap, on an altazimuth head and a three-legged tripod, standing on a ruled floor with its shadow
style: Technical elevation, engraving-style line work
description: An old refracting telescope stands on its tall tripod, tilted at the sky with its finder scope ready. It has been pointed upwards for so long it has forgotten what the ground looks like.

title: Tenement Blocks
subject: Old wooden-framed tenement blocks stacked storey on storey along a narrow lane, deep eaves with upturned tips, balconies and many-paned windows, rows of market stalls with covered roofs down the street below
style: Pen-and-ink street drawing, fine line and light hatching
description: Old tenements climb over a narrow market lane, each storey jutting a little further out than the last. The top floors are close enough to pass a teapot across.

title: Saxophone
subject: One saxophone seen from the side, the crook and mouthpiece at the top, the long body lined with round key pads, rods and guards, the curved bow and the upturned flared bell
style: Instrument study, engraving-style line work, white line on black
description: A single saxophone stands upright in white line, every key and rod along its body drawn in place. It is the quietest one has ever been.

title: Chameleon Study
subject: A single chameleon gripping a branch, side on, with its helmet-like casque, turret eye and curled tail
style: Natural history study, engraving-style pen lines
description: A chameleon grips a branch with split feet, one turret eye on the watch and its casque raised. It is very good at blending in, which is more than can be said for the shirt.

title: Space Rocket
subject: A single space rocket in side elevation, with nose cone, strap-on boosters, swept fins and landing feet on a thin ground line
style: Technical side elevation, engraving-style pen lines
description: A tall rocket stands on its landing feet, boosters strapped to its sides and fins swept back. It has been ready for launch for some time now and is in no hurry.

title: Old Town Street
subject: A narrow cobbled street between tall old houses, a tiered church tower and a thin spire rising behind, in fine pen hatching
style: Pen-and-ink street drawing, fine hatching, edge to edge with a straight ground line
description: A cobbled street curves between tall old houses towards a gate, with a church tower keeping watch above the roofs. The cobbles have outlasted every shoe that walked on them, and will see off yours as well.

title: Espresso Machine
subject: A single lever espresso machine seen from the front, with gauges, bean hopper, group head, portafilter and a long side lever, drawn in white line on black
style: Patent-style drawing, white chalk line on black
description: A lever espresso machine stands square on, gauges up, portafilter locked in and its long lever ready to pull. It is quite capable of making one very good coffee before anyone has properly woken up.

title: Hummingbird Study
subject: A hummingbird hovering with its wings raised and long bill pointed up, two smaller hummingbirds in flight either side
style: Naturalist's study sheet, fine pen and ink hatching
description: One large hummingbird hangs in the air with its wings spread and bill raised, while two smaller ones hover at its sides. They beat their wings dozens of times a second and still find the time to look composed.

title: Vintage Motorcycle
subject: A single vintage motorcycle in side elevation, spoked wheels, teardrop tank, sprung saddle, rear rack and a V-twin engine, on a thin ground line
style: Technical side elevation, pen and ink
description: An old twin-cylinder motorcycle stands in clean side view on a single ruled line, every spoke, fin and pipe accounted for. It has a luggage rack and a seat for one, which settles the question of who carries the shopping.

title: Market Street
subject: A narrow old street of tall stone houses with arcades, balconies and hanging plants, a church spire at the far end, fruit carts and baskets on the cobbles
style: Dense pen and ink street view, the ground cut in a straight line
description: Tall old houses lean over a cobbled lane of arcades and balconies, with a spire closing the view and fruit sellers at work below. The street was laid out long before anyone thought of parking.

title: Microphone Study
subject: A single vintage studio microphone with a ribbed grille on a jointed mount, a short stem and a round weighted base
style: White line on black, engraved-style hatching
description: An old studio microphone stands on its stem and heavy round foot, its ribbed grille drawn bar by bar. It has heard a great many people clear their throats.

title: Beetle Study
subject: A large horned beetle seen from above, six legs spread, with a sheet of smaller beetles and bugs drawn round it
style: Natural history study sheet, fine pen lines and stipple
description: A big horned beetle sprawls across the middle of a collector's sheet, its smaller relatives lined up round the edges. Nobody asked the small ones whether they minded the seating plan.

title: Steamboat
subject: A small steam vessel in side elevation, funnel, wheelhouse and one mast with its rigging, on a thin waterline
style: Technical side elevation, fine pen lines
description: A small steamer sits on a flat calm, one funnel, one mast and a web of rigging pulled taut fore and aft. It has clearly never been asked to hurry.

title: Old Town Lane
subject: A steep cobbled lane climbing between tall stone houses to a spired building at the top
style: Dense pen and ink street scene, fine line and hatching
description: A narrow cobbled lane climbs between tall stone houses towards a spired building at the top of the hill. Every step up is one fewer you will have to walk back down.

title: Globe Study
subject: An antique terrestrial globe on a turned pedestal stand, with its horizon ring and meridian ring, continents and grid lines
style: Engraved instrument study, white line on black
description: An old library globe sits in its horizon ring on a turned pedestal, continents and grid lines drawn across the sphere. It has spent a long career pointing at places it will never visit.

title: Tree Frog Study
subject: A single big-eyed tree frog sitting face on, on a broad veined leaf, its toe pads splayed
style: Natural history drawing, engraving-style pen lines
description: A tree frog sits square on a leaf and looks straight back, round eyes wide and toe pads spread for grip. It has the air of someone who has been waiting for you for some time.

title: Ferris Wheel
subject: A single Ferris wheel seen face on, its spokes, rim and hanging cabins on an A-frame over a small station and a ground line
style: Technical elevation, fine pen and construction lines
description: A Ferris wheel stands face on, its spokes running in to one hub and its cabins hung round the rim. It goes nowhere at great expense and everyone queues for it anyway.

title: Tennis Racket Study
subject: A single tennis racket upright in the centre, strung head, open throat and wrapped grip, with small detail drawings of parts in two columns round it
style: Patent study sheet, white chalk line on black
description: A tennis racket stands at the centre of a patent sheet, its strings and wrapped grip drawn out with a column of parts on either side. None of it will help your backhand, but it does look the part.

title: Snake Study
subject: A single snake coiled in heavy loops, its head raised and turned to one side, every scale drawn
style: Natural history study, engraving-style pen lines
description: A snake lies coiled in thick, finely scaled loops with its head lifted to look over its own body. It has no legs, no arms and no apparent worries.

title: Observatory
subject: A domed observatory on a round, three-storey stone drum, the shutter slit of the dome open along one rib, steps at its foot
style: Architectural elevation, engraving-style pen lines
description: A stone observatory rises in three ringed storeys to a ribbed dome with its observing slit opened to the sky. The building does its best work at night and keeps its curtains open on purpose.

title: Baroque Church
subject: A baroque church front with two onion-domed towers and a third domed tower, a rose window over the arched door, old houses lining the street on either side and a paved square in front
style: Pen-and-ink town view, fine hatching
description: A baroque church front fills the end of a narrow street, its domed towers rising over a rose window and an arched door. The houses either side have been leaning in for a better look for a few hundred years.

title: Rotary Phone Study
subject: A vintage rotary telephone with a finger dial in its square base, a tall column carrying a cradled handset, coiled cords and a few detached parts beside it
style: Patent study sheet, white line on black
description: An old rotary telephone stands tall on its square base, the finger dial below and the handset resting on a cradle above, a spare earpiece and fittings drawn alongside. It takes a full second per digit and has never once sent anyone a notification.

title: Raven Study
subject: A single raven perched on an old broken stump, seen side on, its heavy beak, glossy head and layered wing feathers drawn in fine engraved hatching
style: Natural history study, engraving-style pen lines
description: A raven sits on a weathered stump, every wing feather laid down in close pen hatching. It has the look of a bird that has already decided what it thinks of you.

title: Arch Bridge
subject: An old stone bridge of three round arches seen from the side, a balustraded parapet between two round towers, trees and boulders on both banks and still water beneath
style: Engraved plate, pen lines and hatching in a keyline rectangle
description: Three stone arches carry a balustraded road between two round towers over a quiet river. Whoever built the towers was clearly expecting more trouble than the river has ever given.

title: Canal Town
subject: A narrow canal running between tall old houses with balconies, shutters and tiled roofs, wooden rowing boats moored along the water and a hill town climbing behind
style: Pen-and-ink townscape, fine hatching edge to edge
description: Old stone and timber houses lean over a narrow canal where small wooden boats wait at their moorings. Nobody here has needed to look for a parking space in several centuries.

title: Hiking Boot Study
subject: A leather lace-up hiking boot seen from the side with its eyelets, padded cuff and deep lugged sole, beside the same boot seen from above with its laces crossing the tongue
style: Patent drawing, white chalk line on black
description: A hiking boot is drawn twice, once from the side down to every lug of its sole and once from above with the laces criss-crossing. The plans are thorough; the blisters are not included.

title: Fox Study
subject: A fox sitting upright, three-quarter side view, ears up and brush curled round its feet
style: Natural history study, fine pen and ink fur hatching
description: A fox sits upright with its brush wrapped round its paws, every hair of its coat drawn in fine pen. It is looking at something just out of frame and has clearly already made up its mind about it.

title: Vintage Tractor
subject: An old farm tractor in side elevation: big ribbed rear wheel, small spoked front wheel, bonnet, grille, exhaust stack and steering wheel
style: Technical side elevation, engraving-style pen lines
description: A mid-century farm tractor drawn in clean side view, from its slatted grille to its deep-treaded rear tyre. It has one speed, which is slower than the car behind it.

title: Old Town Bridge
subject: A stone arch bridge over a narrow river between tall timber-framed medieval houses, gables, chimneys and a little tower
style: Dense pen and ink street drawing, fine hatching edge to edge
description: A stone bridge arches over a narrow river, hemmed in by leaning timber-framed houses and their chimneys. The houses have stood there for centuries, mostly by leaning on each other.

title: Fishing Fly Study
subject: An artificial fishing fly seen from the side: a bulbous head, a ribbed body, feather wings and tail, thin legs and a curved hook beneath
style: Patent study sheet, fine white line
description: A hand-tied fishing fly, all feather wings and fine legs, with the hook curled discreetly underneath. It is built to look exactly like dinner, which is the whole point.

title: Mushroom Study
subject: One large spotted mushroom with gills under its cap, five smaller mushrooms round it on a tuft of grass and twigs
style: Natural history plate, engraving-style pen lines
description: A tall spotted mushroom stands over five smaller relations, every gill drawn under its broad cap. Nobody has yet decided which of them is safe to eat, and nobody is volunteering.

title: Lattice Tower
subject: One tall steel lattice tower seen side on, two cross-arms near the top, guy wires running to the ground, low bushes at its feet
style: Technical elevation, ruled ink lines
description: A steel lattice tower rises from a strip of scrub, its girders crossing all the way up to a slim spire. It has stood there a long time without receiving a single compliment.

title: Temple Stairs
subject: A long flight of stone steps with balustrades climbing between pine trees and shrubs to a temple with three curved tiled roofs
style: Dense pen and ink, fine cross-hatching
description: Stone steps climb between twisted pines to the door of a three-roofed temple, every tile and needle drawn. The view at the top is said to be worth it, which is what people say about all stairs.

title: Kite Study
subject: One diamond kite with crossed spars, bridle lines and a knotted tail string, four round detail drawings in the corners
style: Patent study sheet, white chalk line on black
description: A diamond kite spreads its crossed spars in the middle of a patent sheet, bridle lines and tail drawn with care. The drawing assumes a steady breeze, which is the most optimistic thing about it.

title: Humpback Whale
subject: One humpback whale breaching, side view, long knobbly pectoral fin, throat grooves, small eye and a single fluke
style: Natural history plate, black ink line engraving with cross-hatching
description: A humpback whale rises out of the frame with its long pectoral fin swept back and its throat grooves drawn line by line. Forty tonnes, and still it insists on jumping.

title: Ammonite
subject: One ammonite fossil shell in flat side view, a single tightening spiral with strong outward-curving ribs
style: Natural history plate, black ink line engraving with cross-hatching
description: An ammonite coils down to a pinpoint centre, every rib of its last whorl swelling outward towards the aperture. It has kept its shape for some hundred million years, which is more than most of us manage over a weekend.

title: Hot Air Balloon
subject: A hot air balloon in front elevation: a tall envelope of vertical gores with a load band, a net of ropes down to a load ring and a small wicker basket hanging below
style: Victorian patent engraving, fine pen lines and cross-hatching
description: A hot air balloon drawn gore by gore, its rope net gathered to a single wicker basket. Steering remains, as ever, a matter for the wind.

title: Colonial House
subject: An old colonial house with two storeys of deep arcaded verandas, turned columns, railings and shutters, a palm leaning over the roof
style: Pen-and-ink line engraving, cross-hatched, the scene dissolving into the tee at its edges
description: A colonial house shown front-on, its verandas stacked two deep under a pedimented roof and a palm. Built for sitting outside in the shade, which is as much as anyone ever did on one.

title: Lighthouse
subject: A tall tapering stone lighthouse on a rock: glazed lantern and domed cap, railed gallery on corbels, three small windows and the keeper's door at the top of a flight of steps
style: Pen-and-ink line engraving, cross-hatched, in front elevation like an architect's plate
description: A stone lighthouse in front elevation, from the keeper's door up to the lantern and the finial on its domed cap. One tower, one lamp and one man to wind it, which was considered adequate staffing for an entire coast.

title: Oak and Fox Earth
subject: An old English oak in winter cut away below ground: the bare crown above, the roots spreading through the soil below, and a fox earth among the roots with a vixen and her cubs asleep, a tunnel rising to the surface
style: Photographic cross-section in a halftone screen
description: Above the ground, an old oak stands bare for the winter; below it, a vixen and her cubs sleep in an earth among its roots. The tree, presumably, has not been told.

title: Drawn from a Rumor
subject: Albrecht Dürer's 1515 woodcut rhinoceros, the armoured beast he cut without ever seeing one, from a letter and a sketch sent from Lisbon: its head, horn, scaled legs and plated shoulder, with his own "1515 RHINOCERVS" and monogram, and the caption "DRAWN FROM A RUMOR." under it
style: Woodcut line traced from a museum scan, with a classical-capital caption
description: Dürer never saw a rhinoceros. He cut this one in 1515 from a letter and a rough sketch, armour plates and all, and for more than two centuries it was what Europe believed a rhinoceros looked like.
credit: Albrecht Dürer, The Rhinoceros, 1515, woodcut. Cleveland Museum of Art, 1993.9, open access (CC0): https://www.clevelandart.org/art/1993.9. Traced to one ink, cropped and captioned by MONO.

title: Nobody Had Looked
subject: Robert Hooke's 1665 engraving of a flea from Micrographia, shown close: the head with its eye, the plated thorax and the two front legs with their claws, Hooke's plate letters kept, with the caption "Nobody had looked this closely before." under it
style: Engraving line traced from a library scan, with a bold serif caption
description: In 1665 Robert Hooke put a flea under his microscope and engraved what he saw, armour plates, bristles, claws and all. London had never seen anything like it.
credit: Robert Hooke, Micrographia (1665), Schem. XXXIV, the flea. Wellcome Collection, L0084699, CC BY 4.0: https://wellcomecollection.org/works/jrp59aem. Traced to one ink, cropped and captioned by MONO.

title: Pasta: A Field Guide
subject: Sixteen pasta shapes drawn like the plates of a naturalist's field guide, in a four-by-four chart under the heading "PASTA / A FIELD GUIDE", each shape named below it: spaghetti, penne rigate, farfalle, fusilli, rigatoni, conchiglie, orecchiette, rotelle, cavatappi, tortellini, ravioli, gemelli, radiatori, ditalini, campanelle, lasagne
style: Engraving-style line drawing with a serif heading and labels
description: Sixteen pasta shapes, drawn and named the way a naturalist would catalogue beetles. From spaghetti to radiatori, every one is a different answer to holding sauce.

title: Horsepower vs. Poor Decisions
subject: A scatter chart titled "HORSEPOWER VS. POOR DECISIONS": a bicycle, a scooter, a family hatchback, a motorcycle, a 1960s sports car and a dragster climb a trend curve that runs off the top of the print, while a family minivan sits alone well below it
style: Clean line drawings of vehicles on a chart, with a heavy condensed title
description: The more horsepower, the worse the decisions, plotted from a bicycle to a dragster that leaves the chart altogether. One minivan sits far below the curve.

title: The End
subject: The words "the end" in large lowercase type, "end" sitting on the horizon of a calm sea at sunset, with a striped half sun setting just after it, the sun's glittering path on the water, a small sailboat heading out and two gulls, drawn in linocut ripple lines
style: Linocut-style sunset in horizontal ripple lines, with bold lowercase type
description: The closing shot of an old film: the sun goes down on the horizon, a small boat sails off, and "the end" sits on the water. Quiet, and final.

title: Pluto Was Framed
subject: A punk-zine photocopy collage: ransom-note letters cut from different typefaces spell "PLUTO WAS FRAMED"; below, a coarse halftone print of New Horizons' photograph of Pluto, heart and all, taped down on a torn print, with a cut-out of the New Horizons probe, its dotted flight path and a typed label "NEW HORIZONS / 14 JULY 2015"
style: Cut-and-paste ransom note and photocopy collage
description: Pluto was reclassified as a dwarf planet in 2006; nine years later New Horizons flew past it on 14 July 2015 and photographed the heart-shaped plain on its face. The evidence, pasted up like a punk flyer.

title: Making Excellent Progress
subject: A small sloop becalmed at sunset, side on, its mainsail dumped on the boom and its jib hanging slack; the glassy water mirrors it as the same drawing flipped and broken into horizontal dashes that fade with depth. A striped seventies half sun sits on the horizon, its reflection a column of short broken dashes. Below, in letter-spaced monospaced capitals: MAKING EXCELLENT PROGRESS
style: Fine line drawing with a seventies striped sunset
description: A sailing boat is becalmed when the wind dies and it can no longer move under sail; the sails hang slack and still water can mirror the hull. Every sailor has sat through it, and most have said this line over the radio.

title: Nearly Finished
subject: A photograph in halftone of a classic wooden gaff cutter hauled out in a boatyard, seen from the side: the front half of her topsides sanded to clean bare planking, the back half still in old dark paint, chipped and peeling; tape along the waterline, a ladder against her, her mast on trestles behind. Above, in letter-spaced condensed capitals: NEARLY FINISHED, and under it, small: SINCE 1987
style: Halftone photograph with a letter-spaced headline
description: A wooden boat hauled out for a refit is sanded back to bare wood and painted again, one stretch of hull at a time. Some refits take a season; some outlast the people who started them.

title: Four Blows
subject: A 35 mm contact strip running down the back, four frames of the same moustached blacksmith at night, lit only by the forge: pulling a glowing bar from the coal fire with tongs; hammer raised over the anvil, the bar held in the tongs; the hammer landing in a fan of sparks; the bar plunged into a wooden water barrel, thin threads of steam rising. Sprocket holes down both edges, frame numbers 1 2 3 4 in the gaps
style: Halftone photographs in a film contact strip
description: Draw the bar from the fire, raise the hammer, strike, quench. Four frames off one roll, and the whole of a smith's work in each of them. Only what the forge lights is printed; the night of the shop is the shirt.

title: Ketch
subject: A fine pen-and-ink drawing of a two-masted ketch under full sail on still water, seen from the side, bowsprit to the left: firm spars and hull with thin plank lines, the sails light outlines with their seams in rows of round dots, a waterline, broken water lines and a stippled reflection that fades out downward. Above it, light and letter-spaced: KETCH, under it Maritime · Sail plan, over a rule as long as the hull
style: Pen-and-ink sail plan with a letter-spaced heading
description: A ketch carries her sail on two masts, the taller forward, so the canvas is split into pieces a small crew can handle. Drawn here the way a sail plan is: every seam, stay and plank.

title: Wok Hei
subject: A carbon-steel wok mid-toss over a roaring burner at night: a sheet of flame rolls over the lip, fried rice, whole prawns and spring-onion rings hang frozen in the air above it, and the cook's hand grips the handle at the lower right, the arm lost in the dark; the burner fades out at the bottom
style: Halftone photograph, white on black, lit only by the flame
description: The breath of the wok: the second the flame jumps the lip and the rice leaves the pan. Only what the fire lights is printed; the rest of the kitchen is the shirt.

title: Eiger
subject: The Eiger (3,967 m, Bernese Alps) at night, seen from the west-north-west near Kleine Scheidegg: the summit pyramid, the north face on the left in deep shadow, the moonlit west flank on the right running up to the summit, the skyline as a fine line and stars above. On the north face, the headlamps of five rope teams climb towards the summit; the drawing fades out at its foot and sides in an oval vignette
style: Engraving in horizontal lines, white on black
description: The Nordwand at night, with five rope teams' headlamps on it. The mountain is the real one: every line comes from swisstopo's two-metre survey of the Eiger, cut like an old engraving and lit only by the moon.

title: How Beer Is Made
subject: The brewing process as a flow chart of pen drawings under the heading HOW BEER IS MADE: malting, milling and mashing across the top, boiling (with hops added), fermenting and conditioning across the middle, and packaging into bottles, cans and a keg below, each step with its vessel, a heading and one line saying what happens
style: Technical pen drawing with headings and captions, a diagram
description: The whole road from barley to the bottle, step by step: malt, grist, mash, a hopped boil, the fermenter and the conditioning tank. Each vessel is drawn as a brewer knows it and labelled with what it does.

title: Gin Botanicals
subject: A plate of the five classic gin botanicals under the heading GIN BOTANICALS, each with its Latin name in italic: a sprig of juniper with berries (Juniperus communis), coriander in flower with its seeds (Coriandrum sativum), angelica root with a cut slice (Angelica archangelica), a curl of bitter orange peel (Citrus × aurantium), and orris, the iris rhizome with slices and a flower (Iris germanica)
style: Botanical engraving, screened as a fine halftone
description: Juniper, coriander, angelica, bitter orange and orris: the five botanicals at the heart of a classic dry gin. Juniper leads, as it must: a gin is a spirit that tastes first of juniper.

title: Vineyard
subject: A terraced hillside vineyard seen through an arched window under the heading VINEYARD: curving rows of vines held by dry-stone walls climb to a stone farmhouse among cypresses and an olive tree, a hill town on the far ridge; in the foreground vines on wooden posts hang with bunches of grapes over a dirt track
style: Landscape engraving, screened as a fine halftone
description: Terraces of vines climbing a hill to a stone farmhouse and its cypresses, with the harvest hanging heavy in the front row. A landscape drawn the old way, line by line.

title: Barley and Malt
subject: A plate of barley and its malting: an ear of barley (Hordeum vulgare); a barley grain whole and in longitudinal section, its husk (lemma), endosperm and germ (embryo) named; and four grains for the stages of malting, each with a line on what happens: 1. steeping, 2. germination, 3. kilning, 4. malt
style: Botanical engraving, line and hatching, with serif captions
description: Malting in four steps: the grain is steeped in water, left to sprout, then dried in a kiln to stop it, and what is left is the malt a brewer mashes. Above it, the barley ear and a grain cut open to its husk, endosperm and germ.

title: Grapevine (Vitis vinifera)
subject: A plate of the grapevine, Vitis vinifera: a branch with three leaves, tendrils and a hanging bunch of grapes, and a pruned cane with its dormant bud, each with a caption in a serif hand
style: Botanical engraving, line and hatching, with serif captions
description: The grapevine as an old botanical plate: a leafy branch with its tendrils and a full bunch, and beside it a pruned cane with the dormant bud next year's fruit will grow from. Line and hatching, the captions under each part.

title: Fermentation
subject: A conical fermenter drawn in cutaway, its parts named: CO2 to the blow-off, a pressure relief valve, kräusen (yeast foam), fermenting wort, rising CO2 bubbles, yeast in suspension, a cooling jacket and the yeast dump valve; beside it budding yeast cells under magnification, the budding cell, the daughter cell and a CO2 bubble named
style: Technical pen drawing with stipple and captions
description: A conical fermenter at work: kräusen on top, CO2 rising through the wort, and yeast settling towards the cone's dump valve. Beside it the yeast itself under magnification, budding and giving off the gas.

title: Oak Barrel
subject: A cooper's drawing of an oak barrel: its elevation with dimensions (900 mm tall, heads 570 mm across), the stave construction in an exploded view with a stave's sizes (24 staves), the top, middle and bottom hoops, the riveted lap joint and its rivet, and a material key: European oak (Quercus robur / Quercus petraea) staves and heads, galvanised steel hoops, steel rivets
style: Technical drawing with hatching and dimension lines
description: An oak barrel drawn the way a cooper plans one: the elevation, the 24 staves fanned out in an exploded view, the hoops in three pairs and the riveted joint that closes each. Quarter-sawn European oak, galvanised steel, and every part with its size.

title: Pot Still
subject: A copper pot still drawn in cutaway over a wood fire in a brick hearth, its parts named: the fermented wash boiling in the pot, the cut-away neck showing the vapour's path, the swan neck, the lyne arm (vapour pipe), the manway, the worm tub (condenser) with its copper worm coiled in cooling water, cold water in and warm water out, the condensate (spirit) dripping into a jug for the distillate
style: Engraving with crosshatching, arrows and serif captions
description: How a spirit is made in copper: the wash boils in the pot, its vapour climbs the swan neck and runs down the lyne arm into a worm coiled in cold water, and comes out as spirit. A wood fire underneath and every part named, the way the old distillers drew it.

title: Joiner's Tools
subject: A catalogue page of hand tools, each numbered with its size: No. 101 smoothing plane (9 in.), No. 201-204 chisels (1/4, 1/2, 3/4 and 1 in.), No. 301 mallet (head 2 1/2 in.), No. 401 dividers (span 6 in.), No. 501 brace (12 in.) and No. 601 panel saw (22 in.)
style: Catalogue engraving with serif captions
description: A smoothing plane, four chisels from a quarter inch to an inch, a mallet, a pair of spring dividers, a brace and a panel saw, numbered like a page of an old hardware catalogue. The kit of a bench joiner, engraved line by line.

title: Motorcycle
subject: A workshop sheet of a classic motorcycle: its side view with dimensions (1980 mm long, 1330 mm wheelbase, 1000 mm high) and four callouts (side panel, exhaust pipe, engine, seat); details A to E of the carburettor in two views, the front drum brake in section, the rear sprocket, the engine from the right and a rear shock absorber, each with its sizes; and a short table of specifications
style: Technical drawing with dimension lines and typewriter lettering
description: A classic motorcycle drawn as a workshop sheet: the side view with its dimensions, and the carburettor, the front drum brake, the rear sprocket, the engine and a rear shock in detail. Callouts and a table of specifications in a draughtsman's typewriter lettering.
